mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE proxy via labor market weakness) predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day return as weakening demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND UNRATE > previous month by >0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving supply capacity and economic momentum, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to wage and profit growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >100000 AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1,400,000 units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in periods of sustained low HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, regardless of prior level, triggers a risk-off repricing in equities and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative following a >0.75pp FEDFUNDS hike.

mechanism_narrative: A positive co-movement between industrial production (INDPRO) and capacity utilization (implied by INDPRO and RSAFS) above their respective long-run averages over two months signals an overcapacity or overheating supply environment, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > long-run mean AND RSAFS > long-run mean for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of co-elevated INDPRO and RSAFS above long-run means.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months in the absence of a concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO < 0.2% m/m) signals a labor-market imbalance without economic growth, which historically predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to heightened inflation and policy tightening risks.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months AND INDPRO < previous month by >-0.2% (no acceleration)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes.
